title: Apple Rose Tart with Rosewater Glaze
changes_from_base: Thin apple slices packed upright like rose petals in a press-in crust, finished with an apricot and rose water glaze instead of crème pâtissière.
summary: Paper-thin apple slices packed upright in tight rings so the tart looks like a rose, with a fragrant rose water glaze.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, in 1 cm pieces, plus extra for the tin
medium crisp, tart apples such as Braeburn or Honeycrisp (about 450 g)
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: brands vary in strength, so taste

steps.title: Crust
steps.text: pulse the flour, icing sugar and salt, scatter in the butter and pulse to pea-sized pieces. Add the yolk and vanilla, then pulse in water 2 tsp at a time until the crumbs hold when squeezed.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: butter the tin, tip in the crumbs and press them evenly over the base and sides, using the glass for the corners. Keep a walnut-sized piece back for patching. Freeze until hard, about 30 min, while the oven heats to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Part-bake
steps.text: press foil snugly into the case and bake on the tray 20-25 min, until dry and lightly golden. Patch any cracks with the spare dough.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: cut each apple off its core in 3 flat-sided pieces. Slice them into 3 mm half-moons, keeping each piece's slices stacked together. Keeping the slices in order makes building the rose much quicker.

steps.title: Build the rose
steps.text: mix the flour with 1 tbsp of the sugar and scatter over the base. Stand the slices upright, peel edge up, in tight overlapping rings from the outside in, and coil the smallest slices for the centre. Sprinkle the rest of the sugar and the salt down between the slices and dot with the butter.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: 40-45 min, until the apple edges just brown and the crust is deep golden. Cover the rim with foil if it darkens too fast.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: cool 10 min. Warm the jam with a few drops of water until runny, stir in the rose water and brush it lightly over the apples, not the crust. Serve warm or at room temperature. Add the rose water slowly; too much tastes soapy.

tips: A mandoline gives the thinnest, most even slices; always use the guard.
Squeeze a little lemon over the slices if you work slowly.
Pack the rings tightly; the apples shrink as they bake.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep leftovers covered at room temperature for up to 1 day.
